title: Golden Sentinel: divergence detector and rollback policy for batch/cache tuning
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Add an automated evaluation and threshold validator (Golden Sentinel) that gates automated batching/caching configuration recommendations and enables safe canary applies with automatic rollback when quality regressions are detected.
background: Recent cost-optimization work (autotuner for batch/cache) reduced token spend by ~18% on average but produced occasional regressions on rare prompt families. We need an automated, reproducible eval harness and gating logic that ties recommended config changes to acceptance thresholds before applying them to production or dedicated fleets.
problem_statement: How do we safely apply batching and KV-cache recommendations generated by the cost autotuner without causing silent quality degradation? Current manual review is slow and unscalable for frequent recommendations.
proposal: Build Golden Sentinel: a two-stage validator that (1) runs a deterministic offline eval suite (golden prompt set + automated quality checks) on proposed config diffs, and (2) executes a short-canary in-production run with stochastic sampling and automatic rollback if sentinel metrics cross thresholds. Integrate the validator with the config apply pipeline so that only proposals that pass both stages can be auto-applied.
acceptance_criteria: Offline eval runner exists and executes a candidate config diff on the golden prompt set within CI (<=30m runtime for default set)
A set of sentinel metrics is defined (semantic similarity, task-specific correctness, hallucination classifier score, and delta token/latency), with clear pass/fail thresholds
Canary pipeline can apply config to a 0.5-2% traffic slice and collect sentinel metrics for the slice for a configurable window
Automatic rollback mechanism triggers within 5 minutes of threshold breach and records audit trail (who/what/why)
Dashboard in Console surfaces canary vs baseline per-route metrics and flags failed canaries, with links to failing prompts and diffs
implementation_plan: 1) Define golden prompt families and tagging taxonomy (PM + REs + clients). Start with 120 prompts across chat, completion, and rerank workloads
2) Implement an offline eval runner in the autotuner CI that can replay prompts deterministically (seeded RNG) and produce per-prompt metrics
3) Create sentinel metric definitions: embedding cosine delta, task exact-match / BLEU tradeoffs where applicable, hallucination classifier delta, mean latency and token cost delta
4) Build a lightweight canary controller that routes configured % of traffic to candidate config and collects metrics for the window
5) Integrate rollback hooks into serving control plane (api to revert configs + tag canary as failed in audit logs)
6) Add Console widgets: canary summary, per-prompt divergences, and replay links
7) Add policy layer for auto-apply: only configs that pass offline eval AND canary within thresholds are eligible for auto-apply; otherwise require manual review
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal cluster only (dev/dedicated staging) run offline evals to calibrate thresholds (2 weeks). Phase B: low-traffic canaries (0.5%) for 1 route family for 2 weeks. Phase C: increase to multiple routes and expose auto-apply for P1 customers behind feature flag. Finalize runbooks and training for SRE and customer success.
measurement_metrics: Embedding cosine delta (per-prompt median and 95th percentile)
Hallucination classifier rate delta (false positive/false negative monitoring)
Delta token cost and mean latency
Canary failure rate and rollback frequency
risks_and_mitigation: False positives: overly-sensitive thresholds may block useful cost wins -> mitigate by phased threshold calibration and manual override path
False negatives: missed regressions on rare prompts -> mitigate by expanding golden set and adding randomized prompt sampling
Canary noise from traffic skew -> mitigate by traffic stratification and baseline re-centering before comparison
Rollback flapping -> add hysteresis and minimum stable window before re-apply
